balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): the FY2024 drop in equity is not a loss -- it is the ~RMB 9,869m special dividend (cash plus a Feb-2025 scrip issue of 1,042.6m shares) paid out of share premium. That distribution pushed Ping An Group's holding through the 30% Takeovers Code threshold; the ensuing mandatory offer closed in 2025 with Ping An Group at ~53.71% and the company now consolidated as its subsidiary.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Equity moves driven by capital returns/share issues versus retained earnings
  • Related-party terms now that Ping An Group is the controlling shareholder

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted). The company carries zero interest-bearing debt, so WACC = cost of equity in the DCF.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): cash sits alongside a separate, large non-operating treasury book -- term deposits plus financial assets at FVTPL (wealth-management products issued by Ping An AM/WM, a related party) -- that does not appear on this chart. That book was RMB 10.9bn at FY2024, RMB 6.9bn at FY2025 and RMB 4.2bn at H1 FY2026, and it funded the FY2024 special dividend: the board declared a ~RMB 9,869m distribution (cash + a Feb-2025 scrip issue of 1,042.6m new shares in lieu), paid from share premium rather than earnings, which pushed Ping An Group's stake through the Hong Kong Takeovers Code's 30% trigger. The resulting mandatory general offer closed in 2025 with Ping An Group holding ~53.71% and 1833.HK consolidated as its subsidiary -- the single biggest driver of the FY2024-25 swings in equity, cash and the shareholder register, and the reason related-party pricing risk (Ping An Group is now both majority owner and main customer) is charged in the DCF's bear case and bear weighting rather than stacked into WACC.

What to watch:

  • Whether the remaining term-deposit/FVTPL book keeps shrinking as it is distributed or redeployed
  • Related-party pricing terms with Ping An Group now that it is the controlling shareholder
  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA; refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited ("Ping An Health" / "Ping An Good Doctor"): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
